title: Identification of photosynthesis-related genes in peanut (Arachis hypogaea L.) by hyperspectral phenomics, GWAS, and RNA-seq
content:
Abstract
Peanut (Arachis hypogaea L.) contributes importantly to the global food supply, and its yield potential is closely linked to leaf photosynthetic efficiency. However, conventional measurement of leaf net photosynthetic rate (Leaf Pn) is time- and labor-intensive, limiting its application to large breeding populations. We established a phenomics-driven framework integrating hyperspectral reflectance and genome-wide association studies for high-throughput evaluation and genetic dissection of Leaf Pn. Machine-learning models were trained on preprocessed spectral data from 1,200 leaf samples collected in 4 environments. Random forest performed best after Savitzky–Golay smoothing and first-derivative transformation (R2 = 0.81, root mean square error = 1.50), outperforming the vegetation index-based model (R2 = 0.66). Applying this model to a panel of 173 peanut genotypes identified 2 quantitative trait loci, qPn5.1 and qPn13.1, encompassing 7 candidate genes. Integrated analyses prioritized Arahy.K5L3ZW, which encodes protein kinase 2B. Silencing this gene increased Leaf Pn, whereas transient overexpression decreased it, indicating that Arahy.K5L3ZW negatively regulates Leaf Pn. This framework enables high-throughput genetic dissection of seedling photosynthetic capacity and identifies a candidate target for improving photosynthetic efficiency in peanut.
